Case: Sylvester is a 60-year-old with history of prior L5-S1 posterior lumbar fusion who presents with 8 months of new thigh pain. Sylvester states that he was previously in good health and pain-free since his last surgery, but for the last 8 months, he has had progressive discomfort in his anterior thighs. This discomfort has transformed into severe pain in the last 3 months, which he says is worse after prolonged ambulation and often keeps his from sleeping. When you examine Sylvester, you discover bilateral hip flexor weakness and diminished sensation over his anterior thighs and knees. MRI and CT of the lumbar spine show intact instrumentation at L5-S1, but with new degenerative changes at L4-L5 resulting in canal and neuroforaminal stenosis. The findings are consistent with adjacent-level disease.
Question: Would you offer hydrocodone to Sylvester? Yes or No? If yes, how much supply would you give – Low (1 week), or High (4 weeks) supply? Explain.
